subject: Canary traffic safety harness / automatic fallback — approval request
messages:
From: Ethan Mitchell <ethan.mitchell@acme-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Canary rollout assurances for Q1 launch

Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Before we kick off our phased rollout next week, legal and SRE here asked for a short note on how Redwood will handle canary traffic and safeguards to meet the uptime/latency commitments in our SOW. Specifically: 

- We need automatic fallback behavior if the canary exhibits higher latency or error rate (we'd like to avoid manual intervention during our 10% canary window).
- Pinning / version-lock behavior: if the canary fails, we need the ability to pin back to the previous model version automatically.
- A short list of thresholds you'd monitor (error %, p95 latency) and typical time-to-fallback.

I've attached our standard questionnaire and the SOW excerpt. Can you confirm?

Ethan
Ethan Mitchell
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
Attachments: requested_security_questionnaire.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Mitchell <ethan.mitchell@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Canary rollout assurances for Q1 launch

Ethan — thank you for the clear ask and the questionnaire.

Short answer: yes, we support automatic fallback and model-version pinning as part of our Deploy Safety features. I'm looping in Priyom (Customer Success/Program mgmt) and Marcus (Runtime) to capture the exact thresholds and operational runbook. Below is a high-level summary we can include in the SOW amendment: 

- Canary window: configurable percentage (we recommend starting at 5-10%).
- Monitoring & triggers: automatic rollback when either of the following persists for a 3-minute sliding window:
  • Error rate on canary > 1.5x production baseline AND > 0.5% absolute errors
  • p95 latency on canary exceeds baseline p95 by > 200ms AND sustained increase of >10% traffic slowdown
- Action: automatic traffic re-route to previous pinned model variant and cancel further rollout steps.
- Pinning: model version pin operation is atomic and can be backfilled by the control plane; customers can request a manual pin or allow automatic pin on rollback.
- Expected detection-to-fallback timeline: 1–3 minutes (typical) depending on sampling windows and batching.

Next steps: Marcus will provide exact metric names and default values, and Priyom will draft the SOW amendment language and DocuSign flow for your legal team. If Acme has any hard thresholds (e.g., p95 delta must be <= 100ms), flag them now and we'll evaluate.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — making inference predictable
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ethan Mitchell <ethan.mitchell@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Canary rollout assurances for Q1 launch

Ethan / Mina — quick engineering note with the concrete knobs we'll use.

Operational knobs (defaults we propose for Acme):
- Metric names: 
  * redwood.request.error_rate.canary
  * redwood.request.latency.p95.canary
- Baseline computation: rolling 30-minute production baseline sampled at 1-min resolution.
- Trigger logic (configurable):
  * ERROR_TRIGGER if canary_error_rate > max(0.5%, 1.5 * baseline_error_rate) for 3 consecutive 60s buckets.
  * LATENCY_TRIGGER if canary_p95 > baseline_p95 + 200ms for 3 consecutive 60s buckets.
- Fallback action: immediate reroute of new requests to last healthy pinned variant; existing in-flight requests are allowed to complete. KV cache remains compatible if the models are architecture-compatible; otherwise we automatically flush the KV context and fall back with a short inherited latency hit (~50–120ms).
- Safety: automatic fallback emits a high-priority incident to Acme's configured webhook + creates a trace in Console with token-level latency breakdown.

We can tighten the latency threshold to 100ms if Acme's SLO requires it — that'll increase sensitivity (more frequent fallbacks) but reduces risk of user-facing degradation.

Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_canary_policy_v1.pdf
From: Ethan Mitchell <ethan.mitchell@acme-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Canary rollout assurances for Q1 launch

Mina / Marcus — this looks good. A couple of asks from Acme: 

1) We want fallback to occur within 3 minutes for production-impacting events and automatic model pin on rollback.
2) We will accept 200ms p95 delta as proposed but request that we can opt into a tighter 100ms threshold for customer-facing checkout routes.
3) Please include a sentence in the SOW amendment about a 0.5% SLA credit if automated fallback fails to trigger within the detection window for an incident exceeding 5 minutes.

I'll route this to legal; they've prepared an amendment and will send a DocuSign link. Sending now.

Ethan
Attachments: ACME_DocuSign_SLA_Amendment.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Mitchell <ethan.mitchell@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jan 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Canary rollout assurances for Q1 launch

Ethan — thanks, and acknowledged. Final confirmation & next steps: 

- Redwood accepts the automatic fallback + automatic pin on rollback language. We will add an opt-in tighter threshold (100ms p95 delta) for designated customer-facing routes — configuration will live in the Router rules and be editable by Acme admins.
- We'll include the SLA credit clause you requested; legal review from our side (Laura) will add a short operational appendix that lists metric names and the detection windows.
- Priyom will share the amendment draft in HubSpot and we will countersign via DocuSign once both sides approve.

Action items: 
- Priyom: create HubSpot record and upload DocuSign draft (due EOD Thu).
- Marcus: add the opt-in route flag to the rollout config and validate fallback end-to-end in our staging cluster (ETA Fri).
- Mina: coordinate final SOW language and sign-off call.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth launch.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
